_doc: NAMED CONFORMANCE GAPS. A place where busbar's bytes and a vendor's PUBLISHED schema disagree,
the disagreement has been read, and the owner has ruled that the bytes are right and the schema
is the thing that is incomplete. Every entry here turns ONE named violation on ONE named row
from FAIL into the rig's named-gap status (SKIP): still printed, still counted, still excluded
from the owed set, never a PASS. The validator is not touched — it still finds the violation, and
any violation on the same row that this file does not name still fails the row.
An entry is refused at load time unless it names an owner, a reason, the exact rule, a substring
of the violation's own detail, and the explicit list of ledger rows it covers. There are no
wildcards: a gap that could match a rule across a whole dialect is a bypass, not a gap.
An entry that names a row the run JUDGED and did not produce its violation on is STALE, and a
stale entry is RED (run.sh refuses before the verdict). A gap that has been fixed cannot sit here
This file carries TWO sections, read by two loaders. `gaps` (below) is the FAIL -> named-gap
list described above. `expected`/`accepted` (further down, documented under `_comment`) is the
separate SKIP ceiling: the most rows a run may leave undecided, and who signed for each. A row
the validator judged and failed is the first section's business; a row it could not judge at
all is the second's. Neither loader reads the other's keys.

gaps.why: The Anthropic streaming API DOCUMENTS a `ping` event and tells clients they may see one at any point in a message stream; the published schema's MessageStreamEvent union does not list it. Both statements are Anthropic's. Where the two disagree the wire the vendor's own clients are built to read wins, so busbar's Anthropic writer emits the ping when it composes a stream itself (the four cross-dialect egress lanes here); the same-dialect lane passes the upstream's bytes through and so never reaches this. Dropping the event to satisfy the union would make busbar's stream differ from the one Anthropic describes, which is the opposite of what this rig is for.

gaps.detail_contains: ServiceQuotaExceededException is not an error Converse/ConverseStream declare
gaps.why: `ServiceQuotaExceededException` is a real, documented Bedrock Runtime error type that the Converse and ConverseStream operation shapes leave out of their own error unions. It is the one that says what happened here: the caller's budget is spent, and no amount of waiting changes that. Every error Converse does declare would say something false — `ThrottlingException` tells an SDK to back off and retry a request that can never succeed, and `ValidationException` blames the request. The refusal keeps the accurate type and the gap is named instead, because a router that lies about WHY it refused costs the caller a retry storm.

gaps.detail_contains: property 'trafficType' is not declared by the spec
gaps.why: These two rows are not busbar's bytes — they are GOOGLE'S, captured verbatim off Vertex AI (gemini-2.5-flash, us-central1, 2026-09-07) and committed under crates/busbar-llm-codec/src/tests/proto/golden/vendor/. Every response Vertex returns carries `usageMetadata.trafficType` (the ON_DEMAND vs PROVISIONED billing lane), and the pinned generativelanguage discovery document does not declare it, because that document describes the Gemini API surface and this is the Vertex one. The producer and the schema are both Google's, so there is nothing here for busbar to fix: the recording is what the API sends. Naming it keeps the row honest about the ONE thing it is here to prove — that a field carrying billing-lane meaning reaches busbar undeclared — instead of letting it fail for a reason nobody reads.

gaps.detail_contains: property 'createTime' is not declared by the spec
gaps.why: Same recording, same cause as `gemini-vertex-traffic-type`: Vertex stamps every `GenerateContentResponse` with a top-level `createTime` that the pinned generativelanguage schema's response object does not declare. Google's own bytes against Google's own published schema. busbar neither emits nor consumes the field on these rows — it is passing through what the vendor sent — so the disagreement is the schema's to close, not busbar's.

gaps.detail_contains: property 'domain' is not declared by the spec
gaps.why: A grounded turn returns `groundingMetadata.groundingChunks[].web` objects carrying `domain` alongside the declared `uri` and `title`. The pinned schema's GroundingChunkWeb declares the other two and not this one, so Google's live grounding response cannot validate against Google's published grounding schema. Recorded rather than fixed for the same reason as its two siblings: these rows exist to measure the VENDOR, and editing the recording to satisfy the schema would destroy the only evidence that the two disagree.

_comment: EVERY GAP THIS GATE IS ALLOWED TO HAVE, NAMED. A gap is a row validate.py could not decide:
it is recorded SKIP with a reason, printed as DID NOT VERIFY, and removed from the owed set so
the verdict can still judge the rows that exist. That removal is exactly how a gap hides — an
id that stops being checked stops being counted, and a run with one fewer thing verified reads
the same green as a run with one more. So the gaps are declared HERE, and run.sh refuses any
run whose gaps are not the ones this file names, in no greater number than it names.
`expected` is the most SKIP rows a run may produce. `accepted` names them: one entry per gap,
`cells` a regex over the ledger id (`<cell-id>#request` / `#response`, same convention as
testing/shadow-oracle/accepted-gaps.json), plus an `owner` and a `rationale`. An entry missing
any of the three is refused — a gap with no owner is a gap nobody is fixing. A SKIP row whose
own reason is empty is refused too: named means named, on the row.
FEWER gaps than declared is never red — a gap that closed is what this file exists to drive
towards — but it is printed with the instruction to lower `expected`, so the floor only ever
moves down. MORE, or one this file does not name, is red.
A SKIP row reaches this ceiling by TWO roads, and both are declared here.
1. THE RECORDER COULD NOT RECORD THE CELL AT ALL (its own ledger says UNSUPPORTED), so
there is no wire for this gate to judge. Those are the recorder's to close, not this
rig's; when the fixture lands the cell records, the rows go PASS or FAIL on their
merits, and the entry and the count come off. Each is a `needs_fixture` cell in
testing/shadow-oracle/cells.json.
2. THE `gaps` SECTION ABOVE FORGAVE EVERY VIOLATION ON THE ROW. A forgiven row is a SKIP
row like any other, so it must be inside this ceiling as well as named up there: one
section says WHY the vendor's schema is the incomplete side, this one says how many
forgiven rows a run may have. Two signatures on purpose — the `gaps` entry can be
read alone and still not quietly grow the number of rows nobody judged.
Road 2 was missed when this ceiling was first written (2026-09-06): five rows the `gaps`
section already forgave were never counted here, and the job that would have said so was
red at its own self-test, so nothing reported it. Both roads are declared below now.

accepted.rationale: The mock upstream cannot yet fail PART WAY THROUGH a stream — N good events, then an in-band error event — so the recorder reports UNSUPPORTED for this outcome in all six ingress dialects and there is no recorded wire to judge. 12 rows: 6 dialects x {request, response}.

A request that puts a `cachePoint` before a native `document` block — a wire slot that yields no IR block, ahead of one that does — has no fixture in the tree, so the recorder reports UNSUPPORTED and records nothing.

An answer carrying a URL citation — the Responses annotation the published UrlCitationBody flattens onto the annotation object — has no fixture in the tree, so the recorder reports UNSUPPORTED and records nothing.

The happy path whose ANSWER reports `usageMetadata.toolUsePromptTokenCount` — the server-side tool-use token term Vertex bills BESIDE `promptTokenCount` — has no fixture in the tree, so the recorder reports UNSUPPORTED and records nothing. The cell was added with the gemini tool-use billing change (580352724, 2026-09-07) and is `needs_fixture` in cells.json; this ceiling was written the day before and never grew the two rows. 2 rows.

accepted.owner: llm plane owner (via the `anthropic-ping-event` entry in `gaps` above)
accepted.rationale: NOT a recorder gap: these four rows recorded, were judged, and every violation on them was forgiven by the `anthropic-ping-event` entry above — which is why they arrive here as SKIP. The decision and its reasoning live on that entry (Anthropic documents a `ping` event its own published MessageStreamEvent union omits); this line exists so the four forgiven rows are inside the declared count as well as named, and so a FIFTH cross-dialect Anthropic stream lane cannot appear unjudged under the same name. 4 rows: the four cross-dialect egress lanes busbar composes the stream for.

accepted.owner: llm plane owner (via the `bedrock-service-quota-exceeded` entry in `gaps` above)
accepted.rationale: NOT a recorder gap: the row recorded, was judged, and its one violation was forgiven by the `bedrock-service-quota-exceeded` entry above — Bedrock documents `ServiceQuotaExceededException` but leaves it out of the Converse error union, and busbar keeps the accurate type rather than telling an SDK to retry a request that can never succeed. Declared here so the forgiven row is inside the count as well as named. 1 row.
